title: Speed dependent descending control of freezing behavior in Drosophila melanogaster.
source_locator: Results 'Activation of DNp09 neurons induced freezing' and 'Freezing probability upon DNp09 activation depended on speed'; Fig. 6b-g; Methods 'Optogenetic activation'
quote: We found that CsChrimson activation of DNp09 neurons was sufficient to trigger freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of trials
mapping_basis: Paper uses Namiki et al. 2018 nomenclature (DNp09, line SS01540/SS1540); synonyms.csv marks the name 'DNp09' as ambiguous (also the hemibrain name of DNp71) and driver_lines.csv lists SS01540 as AMBIGUOUS DNp09;DNp71; the Namiki-type name and line support MANC DNp09.
stimulation: 627 nm red LEDs, 0.025 mW/mm2 (25 uW/mm2), 10 x 2 s light on / 20 s off; also closed-loop 2 s stimulation triggered at low (<2 mm/s), high (>15) or very high (>20 mm/s) speed
sensory_condition: freely walking in 30 mm (closed-loop: 60 mm) arena, IR backlight; controls raised without retinal
other_cell_types: weak off-target labeling (unspecified; see FlyLight line SS01540)
penetrance: freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of stimulation events; 85% (506/593) at low speed vs 55% (223/403) at very high speed in closed loop
n_flies_note: 80 retinal-fed test flies, 72 controls (open-loop); 50 flies per condition in closed-loop
notes: Freely walking flies (baseline ~10 mm/s) show a brief initial running bout (speed increase, Fig. 6d) followed by freezing during the 2 s light; jumps at light offset. Coded per conventions: freezing -> legs 'no', effect 'stops'; the initial speed increase is a speed change in already-walking flies and is listed as secondary forward_walking, not as leg-rhythm evidence. Freezing classified by pixel change, not leg tracking. Closed-loop speed conditions (Fig. 6g) differ only in freezing probability, so not split into separate records.
